findings.description: Discover nested submodules after resetting their parent, not before. In a fresh worktree, `commands.prepare` can run `git submodule update --init --recursive --remote`, populating outer@B and outer/new-lib while the superproject records outer@A with a different nested layout. This function caches B's paths, then the checkout loop restores outer to A and attempts to update the now-unregistered new-lib path, failing preparation. The inverse also misses descendants: if B omits a still-populated child, restoring A can expose that child without resetting its preparation-created HEAD. Reset and clean populated repositories top-down, re-reading each restored parent's registrations before descending, while retaining the no-fetch restriction. Related sites: internal/pipeline/steps/prepare.go:123 (cleanup ordering), internal/pipeline/steps/prepare.go:261 (cached-path checkout), internal/pipeline/steps/prepare.go:515 (restoration no longer removes newly populated checkouts), and internal/pipeline/steps/test_base_attribution.go:184 (the same cleanup on the base). This violates the recorded-commit preservation promised at docs/src/content/docs/reference/repo-config.md:357; it concerns preparation cleanup, not the explicitly deferred post-rebase resynchronization.

findings.description: Nested checkouts can still be deleted before preparation reports success. Start with an uninitialized outer submodule whose recorded commit contains inner. A prepare hook runs `git submodule update --init --recursive`, then `git submodule update --remote --recursive`; the newer outer commit removes inner. Cleanup's `git clean -ffd` at prepare.go:120 deletes inner as an untracked nested repository before restoring outer. The new traversal at prepare.go:274 consequently discovers only outer, and the non-recursive update at prepare.go:261 restores outer's recorded commit without restoring inner. Snapshot restoration also skips these previously uninitialized submodules, so the success marker is written with inner empty and later commands never rerun preparation. A renamed nested path instead leaves a stale traversal entry that fails the update at prepare.go:278. Git's submodule and clean manuals document the non-recursive checkout and double-force removal behavior. Fix the ordering at cleanupPreparationChanges: restore each populated parent to its recorded commit before discovering and cleaning its children, rather than traversing the preparation-time topology. This must cover both removed and renamed nested paths and uphold the checkout-preservation promise in docs/src/content/docs/reference/repo-config.md:357.

findings.description: Nested paths are collected before their parent checkout is restored. In an initially empty worktree, `commands.prepare` can run `git submodule update --init --remote --recursive`, populating outer commit B where a nested submodule was renamed from the path recorded in pinned commit A. Cleanup collects B's nested path, checks outer back out at A, then attempts to update the now-unregistered path and fails otherwise successful preparation before Test/Lint runs. Related sites: internal/pipeline/steps/prepare.go:261 consumes that stale list; internal/pipeline/steps/prepare.go:123 invokes it during cleanup. Restore each populated parent before discovering and cleaning its descendants, within preparation cleanup only; this does not require the deliberately deferred per-command resynchronization.
